title: Sampling hints and sparse-span hook for edge SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a lightweight SDK hook that emits sampling hints and a sparse-span envelope for edge/mobile clients. Goal is to reduce telemetry volume and preserve high-fidelity context for troubleshooting intermittent failures when devices have limited connectivity.
acceptance_criteria: Edge SDK exposes a single opt-in hook API: addSparseSpanHook(hintOptions) that developers can call with a sampling hint
Hook emits a compact sparse-span envelope (id, parent_id, sampled_hint, minimal tags) to telemetry pipeline when connectivity is available
Sampling hint supports ADVICE levels: always, likely, rare and a numeric weight for per-request prioritization
Server-side ingestion accepts sparse-span envelopes and recreates candidate traces for downstream diagnostics and dashboard backfilling
End-to-end tests demonstrating 10x reduction in average telemetry bytes per session in poor-connectivity simulated workloads
Instrumentation docs and migration guide for existing SDK users included in observability docs
technical_notes: Design: avoid full-span emission on edge; send compact envelope plus optional delta payloads when network permits
We store sparse spans in a low-cost time-series bucket and link them to full traces when a follow-up request arrives with the same trace id
Sampling keys: deterministic hash of user/session + route to keep stable sampling decisions across retries and offline->online transitions
Trade-offs: sparse-span loses stack-level details; we preserve an error fingerprint and minimal tag set to surface regressions, accepting occasional loss of fine-grained span logs
Privacy: do not materialize PII in sparse envelopes; scrub per-company PII rules via sdk scrubber hooks before emission
Pipeline impact: ingestion needs a compact parser and a new sparse_span index; downstream trace-merge job joins sparse spans with full spans for dashboarding
Backpressure: SDK bucketizes sparse envelopes client-side and uses exponential backoff uploads to avoid battery/network storms
